why: A = lemma_3_7_2 (abstract: any family b ↦ L(b) of sc-operators X → Y over a finite-dimensional parameter space, jointly continuous on level 0, with L(0) injective and the family compactness property, is injective near 0). B is the concrete Lemma 3.59 in the setting of Theorem 3.58. A ⇒ B was proved by building the text's family L(b) = P_Y ∘ Df(b)|_X over Bf = B: X and Y become sc-Banach spaces through the splittings (ofSubspace), Df(b) is the sc-operator at the smooth point b (B ⊆ E_∞ by Proposition 1.6, lifted continuously to E₁), and P_Y is the projection of F = Y ⊕ A. The hypotheses come from B's setting: continuity from the sc¹ property; L(0) injective because ker Df(0) ⊆ B, B ∩ X = 0 and A ∩ Y = 0; FamilyCompactness on O = {b ∈ B ∩ U, |b| < r} from CompactnessProp with m = 0, using a uniform operator bound near b₀ and a continuous lift A → F₁ to make the A-component bounded on level 1. Hypotheses (1) (Fredholm, constant index), (3) and C = (B ∩ C) ⊕ X are not needed. B ⇒ A fails genuinely: A is about arbitrary continuous families with the compactness property, which need not be P_Y ∘ Df(b)|_X for any sc-smooth f in the setting of Theorem 3.58.
